quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to shake or wobble?

options.text: Brakes that do not work properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles happen because the motorcycle is loaded wrong, has unsuitable accessories, or has incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see better and be seen by others.
Help you avoid holes and debris on the road.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear without going slow enough?

options.text: The motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle may speed up too fast.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear without slowing down enough, the motorcycle will jerk forward and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: If your chain slips, tightening it may fix the problem. If tightening does not work, replace the chain before riding.

questions.question: A proper lane position can help you do all of the following, except:

options.text: Stay out of other drivers' blind spots.
See better and be seen by others.

questions.explanation: Your lane position affects your safety. It helps you see and be seen, avoid other drivers' blind spots, and prepare for turns you plan to make.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. When your left arm is extended straight out to the side, it means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Which formation keeps riders in a group closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group to stay close while each rider keeps safe space around them. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Always wear reflective and brightly colored clothing when riding. Crashes happen in daylight and at night, so wear highly visible clothing at any time.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen the best?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider stop other drivers from sharing their lane?

options.text: Give dirty looks to other drivers
Ride in the center of the lane
Ride in the left part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves little space on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should check everything listed below, except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle carefully. Look at the rims and spokes to make sure they are not bent, loose, or damaged. Check your tires and all lights too.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Happen to riders with less than six months of experience
Are caused by broken ignition systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Happen to riders with less than six months of experience
questions.explanation: Be very careful when riding a motorcycle that is new to you. Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on that specific bike.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, but not both

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, when following another vehicle you should:

options.text: Keep at least a four-second distance behind the vehicle
Get as close to the other vehicle as possible
Not worry about your following distance
Always ride in the left part of the lane so drivers can see you

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least a four-second distance behind the vehicle
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds between their motorcycle and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if road or weather conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest
Slowly approach the dog, then speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly approach the dog, then speed up
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, downshift and slowly approach it. Once you are close, speed up and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: How can you keep other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane
Ride in the left part of your lane
Ride in the right part of your lane
Swerve side to side in your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, you should see:

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle
The road in front of your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. You may see a little of your arm or shoulder, but focus on the road behind and beside you.

questions.question: When riding at night compared to riding during the day, a motorcycle rider should do everything below, except:

options.text: Stay farther away from other vehicles
Use the high beam whenever possible

questions.explanation: To stay safe when riding at night, slow down and keep more distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Always be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. It will make the motorcycle less stable. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you safely can. Do not use the brakes, as they can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your risk of an accident?

options.text: Follow the vehicle ahead of you very closely.
Do not look ahead. Focus only on your controls.
Let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce accident risk, make yourself visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles. Always look ahead, to the sides, and behind your motorcycle.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake for normal stops.
Use both brakes only on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: For routine braking, what should you do?

options.text: Switch between the front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Always use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.
